post:
<@1166399169188069529> Thank you for the report, and thank you for the detail you sent with it. The device, the Android version, the build you are on, and exactly what you did before it broke are the four things that make a fault findable, and you gave all four without being asked.

The issue is confirmed on our side. Searching more than one reference drops you out of the Bible and leaves you on Today, and nothing you are doing is causing it. It is being fixed, and the fix goes out in a coming build.

We are leaving this thread open rather than closing it on a promise. When the update reaches you, tell us here whether the search holds. Thank you for your patience with it, and for the care you take reporting these.

<@1166399169188069529> Thank you, and this is a well aimed request.

A concordance over Scripture is something we want, and it belongs beside work already promised in this forum: the catena, so that every verse carries the Fathers who wrote on it. Searching one word through Scripture is the straightforward half.

The other half, finding that word in the Fathers' works, is honest to promise only with a limit attached. A search can only reach what we carry, and the patristic library grows verse by verse as public domain translations allow. So a search across the Fathers will be as complete as that library is on the day you use it, and no more. We would rather tell you that now than have you think the app had looked everywhere.

Accepted, then, with no date on it, because doing it properly means the index has to be built once and built right. Thank you for asking with study in view. Closing the thread, and we will say so in the server when it lands.

<@659973930441900070> Thank you for this, and thank you for writing it from where you are standing. A request made from inside the difficulty is worth more to us than a feature list.

Some of it exists already, and you should not have to wait for it. The prayers before and after meals are in the app now, in the prayer rules. The theology library answers a good part of the beliefs question, and the saints are there to be read.

Some of it is promised and being worked toward: catechumen reading, with Philaret's Catechism and Mogila among the first, and a room for the sacraments.

What you have added, and what we had not written down in this form, is the plain-language dictionary and the practical side. What a troparion is. What an akathist is. What the epistle is. How to set up a prayer corner. The things everybody around you already knows and nobody stops to explain. We are accepting that, and it is going on the roadmap as one place a person can be sent on their first day.

We will not promise a date. A careless definition teaches error to the person least able to catch it, so every entry has to be checked before it goes in.

One part we will probably not do: a list of podcasts and content creators. Recommending living voices is a different act from carrying texts, and a name that is sound this year may not stay sound. Books, prayers, definitions, and the Church's own material we can stand behind.

May God bless your journey. Closing the thread, and we will announce it in the server when it lands.

<@1517280112494645360> Thank you, and the instinct behind this is right. Wanting the phone to stop talking while you pray is a good thing to want, and judging by the reactions here you are not alone in it.

We are not going to build the part where Purify closes your other apps. On Android, an app can only do that by asking for powers that let it watch and control everything else on your phone. We are not willing to hold that over anyone's device, and we would not ask you to trust us with it. The app that teaches prayer should not be the app with the most control over your phone.

What we can do is the part that actually helps: a prayer time you set, and a reminder that arrives when it comes. That sits with the prayer rule work already on the roadmap. For the silence itself, your phone's own Do Not Disturb, set for the same window, does it better than we could and answers to you rather than to us.

So the lock, no, and we would rather say why than go quiet on you. The prayer time and the reminder, yes. Thank you for asking for it. Closing the thread.
